name: Content Quality Auditor
description: Score documents, pages, posts, or artefact libraries against a configurable quality rubric and recommend fixes.
author: Simon Owen
coverImageAlt: Seven-facet inspection halo reveals orange flaws in a paper structure with cyan repair pieces queued below.
coverImagePrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: AI.Tedt.org skill gallery cover
Primary request: Depict a blank modular paper artefact inside a seven-facet optical inspection halo; the calibrated light reveals a few orange structural flaws while cyan repair pieces align nearby in clear priority order, a metaphor for evidence-led content scoring and actionable improvement.
Scene/backdrop: quiet slate inspection bay on a warm paper field, minimal and architectural
Subject: one central layered blank-paper sculpture; one unmarked seven-facet glass-and-metal halo around it; narrow cyan inspection light; two or three visible orange flaws; a short descending sequence of fitted cyan repair pieces ready to restore the structure
Style/medium: premium editorial illustration with tactile dimensional detail, cut paper, optical glass, brushed metal, and softly luminous inserts
Composition/framing: exact 16:10 landscape; centered artefact and complete inspection halo fully contained within the central 84% crop-safe area; strong silhouette with calm negative space
Lighting/mood: rigorous, constructive, calm, quietly technical; cyan analytical light with sparing orange fault highlights
Color palette: warm paper #F8F6F0, slate #101820, navy #00446F, cyan #00A9E0, sparing orange #E86027
Constraints: no text, pseudo-writing, letters, numbers, tick marks, score labels, checklists, clipboards, magnifying glasses, logos, trademarks, or watermark; no document UI, dashboard UI, product UI, or Microsoft Fluent branding; no paw imagery or paw logo; no cats or cat silhouettes
Targeted correction: preserve the inspection-halo concept exactly, but scale and lower the complete halo, artefact, flaws, and repair pieces so the highest metal edge and lowest repair piece both sit at least 12% inside the canvas, with broad warm-paper negative space above and below.
